pos.personaBrief: Hard pressing, precise passing and fast counters (verified pressing, transitions, possession facts) mean possession is a tool, not a goal; danger matters more than the ball.

pro.personaBrief: Dynamo countered at high speed with long passes from Demyanenko to Belanov and shot quickly after winning the ball.

est.personaBrief: Universal method with prescribed tasks, yet Zavarov dropped deep and Blokhin drifted wide, so roles were rehearsed but fluid.

lar.personaBrief: A 4-3-1-2 with central playmakers and two strikers, conservative full-backs and no true wingers; Blokhin drifted wide only occasionally.

blo.personaBrief: Hard-pressing style, defending as a unit, two to three players pressing the ball and a high line with Baltacha sweeping.

mar.personaBrief: Marking in 1985-86 is undocumented; later Dynamo sides mixed zonal and man-oriented defending with collective pressing, leaning to spaces and compactness.

pla.personaBrief: Lobanovskyi imposed a scientific model on players and set 14 tasks per opponent after minute study, so the plan was his own but opponent-informed.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic and results-first, scientific and disciplined, though attacking and efficient; 'results stay' (undated).

sis.personaBrief: Collective ensemble subordinated to a common playing idea, with fixed tasks for all including stars and harsh discipline.

jog.personaBrief: Dynamic, intense, pressing side built on fitness plus precise technique; the classic non-running 10 does not fit though Zavarov was technical.

bas.personaBrief: Mix of signings and homegrown nucleus (Baltacha, Bessonov, Mykhaylychenko); the title side relied on seasoned regulars with high appearance counts.

lid.personaBrief: Highly scientific yet harsh disciplinarian; the coach decides and rules apply to all.
